name: Realized kurtosis: long the quintile with the fattest-tailed daily returns over the past 3 months (Amaya-Christoffersen-Jacobs-Vasquez)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 64. Over k = e-62..e (63 daily returns) with mean mu: m2 = mean((r-mu)^2), m4 = mean((r-mu)^4); kurt = m4/m2^2 (m2 = 0 -> ineligible). Long the top 20% (round down) of eligible names by kurt, equal weight 1/N.
rationale: Amaya et al. find realized kurtosis positively predicts next-period stock returns while realized skewness predicts negatively; kurtosis is the one higher moment of the daily-return distribution this registry has never sorted on.
source: Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs & Vasquez 2015, 'Does realized skewness predict the cross-section of equity returns?', Journal of Financial Economics 118(1), 135-167

name: Cokurtosis premium: long the quintile whose returns co-move most with the cubed market return (Dittmar)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 253. EW market r_m(k) = equal-weight mean of ret(b,k) over every eligible name that has bar k (built from universe bars up to e only). Over k = e-251..e: with mu_i, sd_i the mean and sample std of ret(b,k) and mu_m, sd_m those of r_m(k), cokurt_i = mean((r_i-mu_i)*(r_m-mu_m)^3) / (sd_i*sd_m^3). Long the top 20% (round down) by cokurt_i, equal weight.
rationale: Dittmar shows a kurtosis-averse representative investor requires a premium for stocks whose returns rise with extreme market moves (high cokurtosis); the registry has coskewness but not the fourth co-moment.
source: Dittmar 2002, 'Nonlinear pricing kernels, kurtosis preference, and evidence from the cross section of equity returns', Journal of Finance 57(1), 369-403

name: Alpha momentum: long the quintile with the highest 12-1 month CAPM alpha against the equal-weight market (Huehn-Scholz)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 253. EW market r_m(k) = equal-weight mean of ret(b,k) over every eligible name that has bar k (built from universe bars up to e only). Over k = e-251..e-21 (231 daily observations): alpha_i = intercept of the OLS regression of ret(b,k) on r_m(k) (beta_i = cov/var, alpha_i = mean(r_i) - beta_i*mean(r_m)). Long the top 20% (round down) by alpha_i, equal weight. Differs from residual momentum (r24b-lo-residual-momentum: 36-month regression, residual-sum score) by ranking on the intercept estimated inside the formation window itself.
rationale: Huehn and Scholz find ranking on the formation-period CAPM alpha instead of raw return yields a momentum effect that is stronger, less crash-prone and not subsumed by price momentum.
source: Huehn & Scholz 2018, 'Alpha momentum and price momentum', International Review of Financial Analysis 57, 1-19

name: Value-at-risk premium: long the quintile with the largest 5% daily loss over the past year (Bali-Cakici)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 251. Over k = e-249..e (250 daily returns) sort ascending; VaR_i = -(the 13th lowest return) (the 5% empirical quantile, no interpolation). Long the top 20% (round down) by VaR_i (largest tail loss), equal weight.
rationale: Bali and Cakici find stocks with higher historical value-at-risk earn higher subsequent returns, a premium for bearing left-tail risk that survives size, beta and liquidity controls.
source: Bali & Cakici 2004, 'Value at risk and expected stock returns', Financial Analysts Journal 60(2), 57-73

name: Low inflation beta: long the quintile least exposed to weekly changes in 10-year breakeven inflation, weekly (Fang-Liu-Roussanov)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Weekly rank calls. ctx.state.hist = list of {v, close: {s: b[e].close for every symbol in the view}} appended once per call (v = ctx.macro('T10YIE'), latest known by the rebalance close via ctx.macro), capped at 60 entries (drop the oldest). For symbol s: over the last 53 consecutive entries form pairs (dv_j = v_j - v_(j-1), r_j = close_j/close_(j-1) - 1) where both v values are finite and s has a close in both entries; require exactly 52 pairs else skip s. beta_s = OLS slope of r on dv. Long the bottom 20% (round down) of scored names by beta_s (least inflation-hedging), equal weight; fewer than 3 scored -> {}.
rationale: Fang, Liu and Roussanov find the price of core-inflation risk is negative: stocks that hedge inflation (high inflation beta) earn lower returns because investors pay for the hedge, so the low-beta quintile should carry a premium.
source: Fang, Liu & Roussanov 2022, 'Getting to the core: inflation risks within and across asset classes', NBER Working Paper 30169

name: Short-duration premium: long the quintile least hurt by weekly rises in the 10-year real yield, weekly (Goncalves; Weber)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Weekly rank calls. ctx.state.hist = list of {v, close: {s: b[e].close for every symbol in the view}} appended once per call (v = ctx.macro('DFII10'), latest known by the rebalance close via ctx.macro), capped at 60 entries (drop the oldest). For symbol s: over the last 53 consecutive entries form pairs (dv_j = v_j - v_(j-1), r_j = close_j/close_(j-1) - 1) where both v values are finite and s has a close in both entries; require exactly 52 pairs else skip s. beta_s = OLS slope of r on dv. Long the top 20% (round down) of scored names by beta_s (highest, i.e. least negative, real-rate beta = shortest implied cash-flow duration), equal weight; fewer than 3 scored -> {}.
rationale: Goncalves and Weber document a short-duration premium: stocks whose cash flows are front-loaded (low sensitivity to discount-rate rises) earn higher returns than long-duration growth stocks; price-only duration is proxied by the beta to real-yield changes.
source: Goncalves 2021, 'The short duration premium', Journal of Financial Economics 141(3), 919-945; Weber 2018, 'Cash flow duration and the term structure of equity returns', Journal of Financial Economics 128(3), 486-503

name: Treasury auction cycle: long TLT/IEF for the 5 sessions after each month's 10-year note auction (Lou-Yan-Zhang)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. A value returned at bar i is the position held over bar i+1 (from the close of bar i to the close of bar i+1). Auction day A_m for calendar month m = the second Wednesday of m (the 10-year note is auctioned, new issue or reopening, in the second week of every month: 3-year Tuesday, 10-year Wednesday, 30-year Thursday; the calendar rule is fixed a priori and built for every month in the sample). a = the index of the first bar with ymd(bars[a].time) >= A_m. Return 1 at bar i if a <= i <= a+4 for the most recent auction index a (position held from the auction-day close through the 5th session after it); else 0.
rationale: Lou, Yan and Zhang show Treasury prices fall in the days before scheduled auctions and recover in the days after, as dealers demand compensation for absorbing supply; the post-auction recovery is the long-only half of that cycle.
source: Lou, Yan & Zhang 2013, 'Anticipated and repeated shocks in liquid markets', Review of Financial Studies 26(8), 1891-1912

name: VIX-change style rotation: DIA when the VIX rose over the past week, QQQ when it fell, weekly (Copeland-Copeland)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. A value returned at bar i is the position held over bar i+1 (from the close of bar i to the close of bar i+1). Decision bars: bar i is a decision bar if i >= 6 and floor((floor(bars[i].time/86400)+3)/7) != floor((floor(bars[i-1].time/86400)+3)/7) (first session of a new Monday-start week); the state set at a decision bar is held (returned unchanged) until the next decision bar; before the first decision bar return 0. At a decision bar: v = ctx.macro('VIX', i), v5 = ctx.macro('VIX', i-5); up = (v and v5 finite) and v > v5. ctx.state.hold = (symbol == 'DIA') ? (up ? 1 : 0) : (up ? 0 : 1) (QQQ held when VIX fell or was flat, DIA when it rose). Return ctx.state.hold. Only one of the two assets is held at any time; the benchmark stays the equal-weight pair.
rationale: Copeland and Copeland find that after the VIX rises, value and large-cap portfolios outperform growth and small caps over the following weeks, and the reverse after it falls; DIA/QQQ is the closest value-vs-growth pair in the discovery bucket (c1022-macro-22 drove the same pair by real yields, not by VIX).
source: Copeland & Copeland 1999, 'Market timing: style and size rotation using the VIX', Financial Analysts Journal 55(2), 73-81

name: Cross-asset skewness premium: hold the 8 of 25 asset-class ETFs with the most negative one-year daily skewness, monthly (Lemperiere et al.)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY', rank() mode, rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 253. Over k = e-251..e with mean mu and sample std sd: skew_s = mean((r-mu)^3)/sd^3. Hold the 8 lowest skew_s (most negative), 1/8 each. Cross-asset version (equity, bond, commodity, dollar ETFs together); s29-etf-commodity-skewness used only the commodity sleeve.
rationale: Lemperiere et al. show across stock indices, bonds, currencies and commodities that risk premia are compensation for negative skewness: assets with the most negative return skew earn the highest excess returns.
source: Lemperiere, Deremble, Nguyen, Seager, Potters & Bouchaud 2017, 'Risk premia: asymmetric tail risks and excess returns', Quantitative Finance 17(1), 1-14

name: September effect: flat 13 US equity ETFs for the sessions of September, long otherwise
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. A value returned at bar i is the position held over bar i+1 (from the close of bar i to the close of bar i+1). Return 0 at bar i if the UTC calendar month of ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) is September (the position over the next session is skipped when the next calendar day is in September; a Friday-to-Monday boundary error only shifts the window by one session); else 1.
rationale: September is the only calendar month with a negative average US equity return across the long-run record (Siegel; Lakonishok-Smidt); the registry tests Halloween, turn-of-month, holidays and expiration but never the September month alone.
source: Siegel 2014, 'Stocks for the Long Run' (5th ed., McGraw-Hill), ch. 19 'Calendar anomalies'; Lakonishok & Smidt 1988, 'Are seasonal anomalies real? A ninety-year perspective', Review of Financial Studies 1(4), 403-425

name: Crypto illiquidity premium: long the 6 coins with the highest 30-day Amihud price impact, weekly (Zhang-Li; Amihud)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'CRYPTO_DAILY', rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Eligible if L > 31. ILLIQ_s = mean over k = e-29..e of |ret(b,k)| / (b[k].close*b[k].volume) * 1e6, skipping bars with volume 0 (need >= 20 valid bars). Long the 6 highest ILLIQ_s, 1/6 each. Level of price impact, not its change (c1022-crypto-61) and not raw dollar volume (r25-crypto-small-dv).
rationale: Amihud's illiquidity premium transfers to crypto: Zhang and Li find coins with high price impact per dollar traded earn higher subsequent returns as compensation for liquidity risk.
source: Zhang & Li 2023, 'Liquidity risk and expected cryptocurrency returns', International Journal of Finance & Economics 28(1), 472-492; Amihud 2002, 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5(1), 31-56

name: Crypto realized kurtosis: long the 6 coins with the fattest-tailed daily returns over the past 63 days, weekly (Amaya et al. transfer)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'CRYPTO_DAILY', rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Eligible if L > 64. Over k = e-62..e with mean mu: kurt_s = mean((r-mu)^4)/mean((r-mu)^2)^2 (zero variance -> ineligible). Long the 6 highest kurt_s, 1/6 each.
rationale: If realized kurtosis is priced as in Amaya et al., the crypto cross-section, whose return distributions are far fatter-tailed than equities, is where the premium should be largest.
source: Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs & Vasquez 2015, 'Does realized skewness predict the cross-section of equity returns?', Journal of Financial Economics 118(1), 135-167 (transfer to crypto)

name: Crypto coskewness: long the 6 alts whose returns co-move least with squared Bitcoin returns, weekly (Harvey-Siddique transfer)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'CRYPTO_DAILY', rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Candidates = every symbol except BTCUSDT with L > 91 and BTCUSDT present with L > 91 (BTC bars aligned by date; use the last 90 common dates). Over the 90 common daily returns with means mu_s, mu_B and sample stds sd_s, sd_B: cosk_s = mean((r_s-mu_s)*(r_B-mu_B)^2)/(sd_s*sd_B^2). Long the 6 lowest cosk_s, 1/6 each (BTC itself never held).
rationale: Harvey and Siddique show assets with low (negative) coskewness, which lose when market variance spikes, carry a premium; in crypto the market is Bitcoin and the registry's crypto skew test (c1022-crypto-42) used own skewness, not coskewness.
source: Harvey & Siddique 2000, 'Conditional skewness in asset pricing tests', Journal of Finance 55(3), 1263-1295 (transfer to crypto)

name: Sector long-term reversal: hold the 3 of 11 sector ETFs with the worst 36-to-1-month return, monthly (De Bondt-Thaler; AMP value)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: assets = the 11 sector ETFs, rank() mode, rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 757. score_s = b[e-21].close/b[e-756].close - 1 (3-year return skipping the last month). Hold the 3 lowest score_s, 1/3 each. 3-year horizon because sector history starts 2016-09 (AMP's 5-year window would leave < 4 years of decisions).
rationale: De Bondt and Thaler's long-term reversal and Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen's price-based 'value' both predict that the worst multi-year performers mean-revert; the registry tests it for stocks and crypto but never across equity sectors.
source: De Bondt & Thaler 1985, 'Does the stock market overreact?', Journal of Finance 40(3), 793-805; Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013, 'Value and momentum everywhere', Journal of Finance 68(3), 929-985

name: Crypto size rotation on VIX changes: Bitcoin only in weeks after the VIX rose, equal-weight alts after it fell (Copeland-Copeland transfer)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'CRYPTO_DAILY', rank() mode, rebalance weekly. ctx.state.hist = list of v = ctx.macro('VIX') (latest known by the rebalance close) appended once per call, capped at 8. If fewer than 2 finite entries -> {}. up = hist[last] > hist[last-1]. If up: return {BTCUSDT: 1}; else: return equal weight 1/N over every symbol in the view except BTCUSDT (N = count).
rationale: Copeland and Copeland's finding that large caps beat small caps after volatility rises maps onto crypto's Bitcoin-versus-alts split; existing BTC-vs-alt tests key off BTC's own trend or dominance, never off equity-market fear changes.
source: Copeland & Copeland 1999, 'Market timing: style and size rotation using the VIX', Financial Analysts Journal 55(2), 73-81 (transfer to crypto)

name: Crypto first-half-of-month: long all 18 coins from the month-end close through the 15th, flat in the second half (Ariel transfer; Kaiser)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. A value returned at bar i is the position held over bar i+1 (from the close of bar i to the close of bar i+1). Return 1 at bar i if the UTC day-of-month of ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) is <= 15 (so the position is held from the last close of the month through the close of the 15th); else 0.
rationale: Ariel showed US equity returns accrue almost entirely in the first half of the calendar month; crypto trades on a UTC calendar with monthly salary and fund-flow cycles, and the registry's crypto calendar tests cover turn-of-month and month-of-year but not the half-month split.
source: Ariel 1987, 'A monthly effect in stock returns', Journal of Financial Economics 18(1), 161-174; Kaiser 2019, 'Seasonality in cryptocurrencies', Finance Research Letters 31, 232-238

name: Within-sector low volatility: the least volatile fifth of each sector, equal weight, monthly (Baker-Bradley-Taliaferro micro component)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. SECTOR = the sector map constant copied verbatim from research/hunt2/strategies/r24b-mom-within-sector.mjs (11 groups: tech, comm, discretion, staples, energy, financials, health, industrials, materials, utilities, reits); names absent from the map are ineligible. Rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 253 and SECTOR[s] defined. vol_s = sample std of ret(b,k) over k = e-251..e. Within each sector with >= 5 eligible names pick the lowest max(1, round(0.2*count)) by vol_s; weight every pick equally (1/total picks). Sector-neutral by construction, unlike r24b-lo-low-vol-direct.
rationale: Baker, Bradley and Taliaferro decompose the low-risk anomaly and find a large 'micro' component from selecting low-risk stocks within industries, separate from the 'macro' industry/country tilt that a plain low-vol sort mostly captures.
source: Baker, Bradley & Taliaferro 2014, 'The low-risk anomaly: a decomposition into micro and macro effects', Financial Analysts Journal 70(2), 43-58

name: Low inflation-beta sectors: hold the 4 of 11 sector ETFs least exposed to weekly breakeven-inflation changes, weekly (Fang-Liu-Roussanov)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: assets = the 11 sector ETFs, rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Weekly rank calls. ctx.state.hist = list of {v, close: {s: b[e].close for every symbol in the view}} appended once per call (v = ctx.macro('T10YIE'), latest known by the rebalance close via ctx.macro), capped at 60 entries (drop the oldest). For symbol s: over the last 53 consecutive entries form pairs (dv_j = v_j - v_(j-1), r_j = close_j/close_(j-1) - 1) where both v values are finite and s has a close in both entries; require exactly 52 pairs else skip s. beta_s = OLS slope of r on dv. Hold the 4 lowest beta_s, 1/4 each; fewer than 4 scored -> {}. Estimated betas, unlike c1022-macro-20's a-priori reflation/disinflation baskets; breakevens, unlike the real-yield static tilts.
rationale: Fang, Liu and Roussanov find the negative price of inflation risk shows up across asset classes and industries: sectors that hedge inflation expectations earn lower returns, so the low-beta sectors should carry the premium.
source: Fang, Liu & Roussanov 2022, 'Getting to the core: inflation risks within and across asset classes', NBER Working Paper 30169

name: 'Sell Rosh Hashanah, buy Yom Kippur': flat 13 US equity ETFs between the two holidays, long otherwise (Frieder-Subrahmanyam)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. A value returned at bar i is the position held over bar i+1 (from the close of bar i to the close of bar i+1). Holiday windows [RH, YK] (Rosh Hashanah day through Yom Kippur day, Gregorian, fixed a priori): 2016-10-03..2016-10-12, 2017-09-21..2017-09-30, 2018-09-10..2018-09-19, 2019-09-30..2019-10-09, 2020-09-19..2020-09-28, 2021-09-07..2021-09-16, 2022-09-26..2022-10-05, 2023-09-16..2023-09-25, 2024-10-03..2024-10-12. Return 0 at bar i if ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) falls inside any window (inclusive), else 1. A distinct effect from c1024-acad3-13: the window is a 10-day religious-holiday span that lands in late September or early October, not the calendar month.
rationale: Frieder and Subrahmanyam document significantly lower returns and volume around Yom Kippur and higher returns before Rosh Hashanah, consistent with reduced participation by a subset of market makers and traders; the Wall Street saying has never been tested here.
source: Frieder & Subrahmanyam 2004, 'Nonsecular regularities in returns and volume', Financial Analysts Journal 60(4), 29-34

name: Left-tail momentum: long the quintile with the smallest expected shortfall over the past year (Atilgan-Bali-Demirtas-Gunaydin)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close - 1; windows are counted back from e; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; fewer than 3 picks -> return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rank() mode. Rebalance monthly. Eligible if L > 251. Over k = e-249..e sort the 250 daily returns ascending; ES_i = -(mean of the 12 lowest). Long the bottom 20% (round down) by ES_i (smallest left tail), equal weight. Pre-registered as the opposite-sign counterpart of c1024-acad3-05: Bali-Cakici (2004) predict high-VaR names win, Atilgan et al. (2020) predict they lose; both are run once.
rationale: Atilgan et al. find left-tail risk persists and investors underreact to it, so stocks with large recent tail losses keep earning low returns ('left-tail momentum'); the low-tail quintile is the long leg.
source: Atilgan, Bali, Demirtas & Gunaydin 2020, 'Left-tail momentum: underreaction to bad news, costly arbitrage and equity returns', Journal of Financial Economics 135(3), 725-753

name: Treasury auction cycle, both legs: short TLT/IEF for the 5 sessions into each 10-year auction, long for the 5 after (Lou-Yan-Zhang)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. A value returned at bar i is the position held over bar i+1 (from the close of bar i to the close of bar i+1). Auction day A_m for calendar month m = the second Wednesday of m (the 10-year note is auctioned, new issue or reopening, in the second week of every month: 3-year Tuesday, 10-year Wednesday, 30-year Thursday; the calendar rule is fixed a priori and built for every month in the sample). a = the index of the first bar with ymd(bars[a].time) >= A_m. Let d = ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) (the session the returned position is held over) and A = the auction date of d's calendar month if d <= A, else the auction date of the following month. Return -1 if A-7 <= d <= A-1 (calendar days; the pre-auction concession, about 5 sessions). Return +1 if a <= i <= a+4 for the most recent auction index a (as in c1024-acad3-09). Otherwise 0 (the auction session itself is flat). longShort: true.
rationale: Lou, Yan and Zhang's full cycle is a price decline into the auction and a recovery after it; the long-only version (c1024-acad3-09) captures half, this variant trades both halves and is the paper's own design.
source: Lou, Yan & Zhang 2013, 'Anticipated and repeated shocks in liquid markets', Review of Financial Studies 26(8), 1891-1912
